skill.name: EscalationDiagnosis_v2
skill.initiation: IF a completed Remove action requires follow-up OR an unresolved case has new evidence AND the evidence version has changed OR a flagged PID is present AND the host has not been previously reviewed with the same evidence version
policy: Step 1: Select the exact open-case host needing diagnosis, including earlier alerts retained while another action was busy, ensuring the evidence version is current and the host has not been previously reviewed with unchanged evidence.

Step 2: Analyse the pending evidence version and inspect the returned file indicators after completion, ensuring the analysis is only performed on new or changed evidence and not on unchanged, already reviewed versions.

Step 3: If observed escalate.sh/escalate.exe justifies Restore, or observed cmd.sh/cmd.exe before any response justifies Remove, proceed with action only after confirming the evidence is new or unreviewed. A repeated old cmd file after Remove alone does not justify Restore.
skill.termination: Stop IF the analysis result has been reviewed, a response has been indicated, or analysis failed and requires reassessment, ensuring no repeated analysis on unchanged evidence and no unnecessary actions on hosts with resolved or unchanged cases.

skill.name: EscalationDiagnosis_v2
skill.initiation: IF a completed Remove action requires follow-up OR an unresolved case has new evidence that has not been analyzed AND the evidence version has changed OR a flagged PID is present AND the host has not been previously analyzed with the same evidence version
policy: Step 1: Select the exact open-case host needing diagnosis, prioritizing hosts with flagged PIDs, unresolved evidence, or changed evidence versions. Avoid hosts with unchanged, already reviewed evidence.

Step 2: Analyze the pending evidence version and inspect the returned file indicators. If the evidence version is unchanged and already reviewed, do not repeat analysis. Stop if the result has been consumed and no further action is needed.

Step 3: If escalate.sh/escalate.exe is observed, justify Restore; if cmd.sh/cmd.exe is observed before any response, justify Remove. Avoid Restore based solely on old cmd files after a Remove action. Only perform new actions if new evidence or unresolved cases are confirmed.
skill.termination: Stop IF the analysis result is reviewed, a response is indicated, or analysis failed and requires reassessment. Ensure all steps are completed and no further action is needed based on the evidence version and host review status.

old_skill.name: RiskBasedInvestigation
old_skill.initiation: An available agent has an investigation_due connection lead on an assigned host, without a higher-priority unresolved local case. Connection INFO is uncertain activity, not confirmed compromise.
policy: Read retained investigation_leads and current connection INFO. Choose one exact assigned host with investigation_due=true. Respect the recorded 16-step review cooldown and 32-step lead expiry; never sweep hosts without a lead.
Analyse this host once to obtain information even when Monitor has not flagged a PID. Inspect the actual completed file result; do not keep waiting after the agent is FREE.

For newly supported user compromise, Remove and check the outcome. For observed admin privilege indicators, Restore and inspect completion. An old cmd file alone is not a new attacker and does not justify Restore.

Once the evidence has been reviewed and any indicated response dispatched, stop. Avoid repeated analysis of the same unchanged lead inside the cooldown and avoid discretionary decoys while a useful investigation or response is pending.
old_skill.termination: One justified investigation and any indicated response have completed and their results were reviewed, or the lead no longer warrants intervention.

old_skill.name: RapidProcessResponse
old_skill.initiation: An assigned host has a newly flagged process PID or observed user compromise that has not yet received a response for this evidence version.
policy: Read the host-specific open case, flagged PID, evidence age, and prior outcomes; never confuse a peer's alert with local proof.
For a freshly Monitor-flagged local PID, promptly Remove on that exact host rather than first spending another Analyse turn merely to rediscover the same warning.

A TRUE Remove result only certifies completion. When available, review the case and Analyse once to check privilege escalation or remaining indicators; use PrivilegedRecovery if admin indicators are observed.
Do not Remove again on the same historical file alone. Wait automatically during IN_PROGRESS; make a fresh decision as soon as completion is observable.
old_skill.termination: The flagged evidence has received a response and its follow-up has been reviewed, or privileged recovery is needed.

old_skill.name: SelectiveDeception
old_skill.initiation: There is no outstanding local compromise response or verification, and a valid assigned host without an already successful own decoy is useful for one deliberate deployment.
policy: Prioritize open local threat cases over discretionary deception; select an exact assigned host only after reading the case ledger.
DeployDecoy once on a suitable host lacking a recorded successful own deployment. Do not spread or repeat decoys simply to remain active.
Use the returned deployment status to verify execution; do not Analyse merely to prove that a completed decoy exists.
After success stop. Reattempt a failure only after its observed cause or relevant evidence changes; quiet Sleep is a valid choice.
old_skill.termination: Deployment completed or failed and its status has been inspected, or an urgent threat case needs attention.

old_skill.name: NetworkContainment
old_skill.initiation: Observed threat-origin bits or confirmed local compromise support a specific cross-zone containment decision; the peer busy bit alone is not a threat.
policy: Read the explicitly decoded peer identities and threat-origin bits, current mission phase, and local case evidence.
Use BlockTrafficZone only for a justified, exact destination subnet. Preserve availability by avoiding broad repeated blocks without new evidence.
Record the actual result, stop after reassessing it, and leave recovery to a later evidence-based decision.
old_skill.termination: The targeted block result has been reviewed or the observable containment trigger no longer applies.

old_skill.name: PrivilegedRecovery
old_skill.initiation: An unresolved assigned-host case contains observed admin privilege-escalation file indicators and no later successful Restore for that evidence.
policy: Identify the exact host with observed escalate.sh/escalate.exe; peer severity or ordinary connection INFO alone is insufficient.
Restore that host promptly. Remove cannot terminate privileged root/SYSTEM persistence; repeated Analyse cannot repair it.
Account for the Restore availability cost, but do not indefinitely defer recovery of confirmed admin compromise solely because recovery is disruptive.
Wait for completion and inspect TRUE/FALSE. A successful Restore completes this workflow; only new observed evidence reopens it.
old_skill.termination: Restore completed and its status was read, or recovery failed and requires reassessment.
